questions.question: An MRI identifies a lesion in a large ovoid gray matter mass lying above the hypothalamic sulcus. Which structure is affected?
questions.explanation: The thalamus is the largest diencephalic subdivision and lies above the hypothalamic sulcus.

questions.question: A tumor involves both the medial and lateral geniculate bodies. Which subdivision of the diencephalon is affected?
questions.explanation: The medial and lateral geniculate bodies constitute the metathalamus.

questions.question: Imaging reveals a mass involving the pineal gland and nearby habenular structures. Which diencephalic subdivision contains these structures?
questions.explanation: The epithalamus includes the pineal gland and habenular structures.

questions.question: A small lesion is localized to a group of gray matter nuclei between the thalamus and midbrain. Which region is involved?
questions.explanation: The subthalamus lies between the thalamus and midbrain.

questions.question: A radiologist describes a lesion involving the expanded posterior end of the thalamus, which overhangs the geniculate bodies. What is this part called?
questions.explanation: The pulvinar is the expanded posterior end of the thalamus.

questions.question: A thalamic mass extends laterally and reaches a major white matter pathway immediately adjacent to the thalamus. Which structure is most likely involved?
options: Posterior limb of the internal capsule
questions.explanation: The posterior limb of the internal capsule lies lateral to the thalamus.

questions.question: During third ventricular endoscopy, a bridge of tissue is seen connecting the medial surfaces of the two thalami. What is this structure?
questions.explanation: The interthalamic adhesion connects the medial surfaces of the thalami when present.

questions.question: A patient has a lesion involving the mammillary bodies and infundibular region. Which diencephalic subdivision is primarily involved?
questions.explanation: The mammillary bodies and infundibular region belong to the hypothalamus.
